title: Backend pods can never become Ready: the probe's Host is refused
description:
Found by a deployment review of docs/deployment.md on 2026-08-22, reading the chart rather than a cluster.

infra/helm/inventory-tng/templates/backend-deployment.yaml probes /api/healthz with a plain httpGet and no Host header, so the kubelet sends 'Host: <podIP>:8000'. DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS is set from django.allowedHosts, which names the ingress host and not the pod IP, and settings.py has no wildcard. Django answers 400.

Verified against the real settings module: DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=inventory.nycmesh.net gives ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['inventory.nycmesh.net'], and a probe carrying 'Host: 10.42.0.17:8000' is refused.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the whole deployment: every backend pod starts, fails readiness at once, never joins the Service, and is killed by liveness at roughly 70 seconds. CrashLoopBackOff for ever. The ingress answers 503 because the frontend can proxy to no endpoint. 'kubectl exec' to make the first administrator lands in a container that is killed mid-command. The logs show 400 with no explanation, because DisallowedHost is only visible with DEBUG on, which must not be on.

It is silent, it looks like a database problem, and it is not.

FIX: set the probes' Host header to an allowed host -- the first entry of django.allowedHosts -- on BOTH probes. Then say so under 'Health checks' in docs/deployment.md, because the next person to edit django.allowedHosts will otherwise re-break it.
close_reason: Closed

title: The backend job has been red since before this batch
description:
CI's backend job sets only DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and DATABASE_URL, so DEBUG is False and settings.py selects CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage. collectstatic never runs in that job, so every test that renders /api/docs, /admin/... or the MFA pages dies on 'Missing staticfiles manifest entry'.

Reproduced locally with DJANGO_DEBUG=false: test_only_an_existing_administrator_can_reach_the_grant and test_the_admin_can_still_be_read both fail. With the repository .env, which sets DJANGO_DEBUG=true, all 446 pass.

main has been failing this job since 'Require one issue per commit', and it is a required check, so nothing can merge until it is fixed.

The integration job already sets DJANGO_DEBUG: true for the same reason. The settings comment says the DEBUG split exists because collectstatic has not run in a development checkout, which is what the backend job is.
acceptance_criteria: The backend job passes on main without weakening what the suite covers.
close_reason: The backend job sets DJANGO_DEBUG so the suite runs against a checkout's storage rather than the built image's manifest, which is what the integration job already does.

title: Rework the local landing gate
description: .claude/hooks/landing-gate.sh blocks publishing until a review has been recorded, which is the opposite of the new ordering: quality gates then publish, and review afterwards against the pull request. It also assumes one review per change rather than one per batch. Move the gate onto the merge instead. Separately, its textual test matches any command whose text contains 'git' followed by the words it guards, so prose about this very workflow trips it.
close_reason: The gate now guards the merge rather than the push, keyed on the pull request head, and its command matcher no longer trips on prose. Local file, gitignored.

title: Document how work reaches main
description: New canonical section in DEVELOPERS.md covering the branch, the pull request, publishing before review, the review cycle against the PR, and why rebase is the only merge. Update its Commits section for the trailer and summary rules, replacing 'Several issues at once'. Record the reasoning in docs/decisions/0017. Everything else links here and restates nothing.
close_reason: DEVELOPERS.md gained a canonical Pull requests section; Commits updated for the trailer and summary rules; ADR 0017 records the reasoning.

title: Make Django settings environment-driven
description: Scaffold settings hardcode SECRET_KEY, DEBUG=True, ALLOWED_HOSTS=[] and sqlite. Production deploy is impossible until settings read from env. Add django-environ, .env.sample, Postgres via DATABASE_URL, and wire DRF/CORS/spectacular into INSTALLED_APPS (DRF is installed but unregistered).
acceptance_criteria: No secrets in source; DEBUG defaults False; DATABASE_URL drives Postgres; .env.sample documents every var
close_reason: Closed

title: The landing gate is not in the repository, and fails open three ways when it is
description:
AGENTS.md now lets an agent merge without asking, and names the recorded review cycle as the condition that makes that safe. That condition rests on .claude/hooks/landing-gate.sh, which is weaker than the rule assumes. All verified:

NOT IN THE REPOSITORY. .gitignore:45 ignores .claude/hooks/, and 'git ls-files .claude/' returns only settings.json and skills. The tracked .claude/settings.json is {"hooks": {}}; the PreToolUse registration lives in gitignored .claude/settings.local.json at an absolute /home/lotia path. A fresh clone, a fork, a CI runner and every .claude/worktrees/agent-* checkout get the permission and none of the mechanism. AGENTS.md is CLAUDE.md, CODEX.md and GEMINI.md by symlink, and Codex and Gemini run no Claude Code hooks at all.

RECORD VERIFIES NOTHING. landing-gate.sh:44-59 stamps whatever head gh reports and writes stages: ["code-review", "simplify"] as a hardcoded literal. An agent that has run no review at all can record and merge.

FAILS OPEN THREE WAYS. set -uo pipefail with no -e. jq missing: deny() emits nothing and exits 0, permitting a merge with no receipt. python3 missing: the matcher's stderr is discarded and an empty verdict is read as nothing-to-guard. gh failing, rate-limited or unauthenticated: pr_head() swallows the error with 2>/dev/null, current is empty, and the head comparison at line 199 is skipped -- so a receipt from a superseded head permits the merge. Nothing surfaces that the gate has stopped working.

BYPASSED BY ORDINARY INDIRECTION. The matcher only sees the literal token gh in command position: gh api -X PUT .../merge, env gh, command gh, /usr/bin/gh, bash -c, and a pipe into xargs all walk past it. The script concedes this ('a guardrail, not a security boundary'), which was a fair trade only while a human ask was the real control. It no longer is.
design: Decide what this is meant to be. As a guardrail against forgetting it is fine as it stands and the rule should not lean on it. As the thing that makes merge-without-asking safe it has to be tracked, wired in .claude/settings.json rather than a gitignored local file, fail closed on every missing dependency, and record evidence that the stages ran rather than a literal. Those are different pieces of work and the first question is which one is wanted.
acceptance_criteria: The gate ships with the repository and is wired in tracked settings; a missing jq, python3 or gh denies rather than permits; record stores evidence rather than a hardcoded literal; a test covers each failure mode. Or: AGENTS.md stops claiming the gate is what makes merging safe.

title: EPIC: OpenTelemetry throughout, and logging as an acceptance criterion for all new work
description:
This repository has no observability of any kind. Established by reading it, not assumed:

- settings.py configures no LOGGING and no ADMINS, so nothing Django logs reaches any destination with DEBUG=false (inventory-tng-zya covers the immediate bug)
- there is not one getLogger in the application code
- DRF configures no logging of its own; it is not something that arrives with the framework
- there are no metrics anywhere: no /metrics, no counters, no timings. /api/healthz executes a trivial query and says ok
- the frontend has exactly one console.error, in scan/decodeLoop.ts. It runs in a volunteer's browser and is seen by nobody
- OpenTelemetry appears in the tree only as a transitive Playwright dev dependency

GOAL, as stated by Ali on 2026-08-22: extensive telemetry -- logs AND metrics -- dispatched over OTLP so any OTel-compatible destination can receive it, with the ability to follow one request from a click in the frontend through nginx into Django and its queries, switched on by a debug flag in the frontend. Plus enforcement: after the retrofit lands, every new piece of work is expected to be logged and instrumented, as a Definition of Done item that tooling checks rather than a habit.

This is an epic and its children are not yet written: the design is under review with Ali before anything is decomposed. Do not start work from this issue -- it is the placeholder the review hangs off.
design: Under review. Shape being proposed: OTel SDK in the backend started post-fork under gunicorn; OTel web SDK in the frontend behind a runtime flag; W3C traceparent propagated across the fetch boundary and through nginx; one OTLP endpoint configured by environment, collector-agnostic. Enforcement by a guardrail checker rather than by review attention.
notes: Ali asked to review this extensively before it is broken down. Examples of prior art and a written explanation of the mechanism were requested as part of that review.

title: Every traceback is lost in production: Django's default logging has nowhere to send them
description:
settings.py configures no LOGGING and no ADMINS, so Django's DEFAULT_LOGGING applies. Its two handlers are mutually exclusive by design:

- console  -- filter require_debug_true
- mail_admins -- filter require_debug_false, and needs ADMINS

DEBUG must be false in production, so console is filtered out; ADMINS is empty, so AdminEmailHandler sends nothing. Every record on the django logger and its children therefore reaches no destination at all.

CONSEQUENCE. django.request logs unhandled exceptions at ERROR with exc_info. In production that traceback is written nowhere. What a deployment actually sees is gunicorn's access line -- 'POST /api/... 500' -- with no stack, no exception type, and no request context. The same silence hid DisallowedHost for the whole of inventory-tng-adj: verified by putting a bad Host to the real settings module with DEBUG=False, which answers 400 and writes nothing.

Also lost: django.security.* (host and CSRF failures), django.db.backends warnings, and anything the application logs once it starts logging.

This is scoped deliberately small -- give Django a LOGGING block that writes structured records to stdout, where a container runtime can collect them, and cover it with a test. The full telemetry story is a separate piece of work and should not hold this up.
acceptance_criteria: A LOGGING setting sends WARNING and above -- including django.request tracebacks and django.security -- to stdout with DEBUG=False. A test asserts a traceback reaches a handler under DEBUG=False. docs/deployment.md says where a deployment reads them.

title: Deleting an item or a location destroys stickers already on shelves
description:
Found by an inventory administrator reading guides/administrator.md on 2026-08-22.

Label.item and Label.location are on_delete=CASCADE, while StockMovement's links are PROTECT. So an item or location that has never moved stock CAN be deleted from Django's admin -- the red Delete button is on both pages, since only AppendOnlyAdmin and StagedAdmin refuse deletion -- and doing so silently destroys every Label row pointing at it.

Those codes are printed on stickers that are already on shelves. The code is opaque, so it cannot be worked out again, and Label.code is unique and unchangeable by design. Scanning one afterwards resolves to nothing, for ever.

The guide said 'there is no delete, and there should not be'. It was wrong about the button and right about the intent; it has been corrected to warn instead. This issue is the guard that should make the warning unnecessary.

FIX, to be argued: PROTECT rather than CASCADE, or refuse deletion in the admin for any row a live label points at, so that retiring is the only way out. Whichever, it needs a test that a label survives an attempt on the item it names.

title: An item's search does not read its identifiers, so the table does nothing
description:
Found twice on 2026-08-22, independently: by the rule-1 codebase survey for inventory-tng-65l, and by an inventory administrator reading guides/administrator.md and trying to act on it.

ItemFilter.search in backend/src/inventory/views.py is CharFilter(field_name='name', lookup_expr='icontains'). ItemIdentifier is imported by no serializer and no view; there is no endpoint that returns one. A scan resolves a LABEL code, not an identifier.

So the whole point of the identifier table -- 'a volunteer types what they call the thing and it resolves' -- is not true of the app a volunteer uses. It is true only of Django's admin, whose ItemAdmin.search_fields includes identifiers__value.

That makes docs/data-model.md's 'a scan or a typed string resolves to exactly one item' a statement about an intention. guides/administrator.md said the same thing and has been corrected to what is true today; this issue is the code that would make the original sentence honest.

DEPENDS ON THE RULE 1 DESIGN. inventory-tng-65l decision 6 already settled how this has to be indexed: add text_pattern_ops on the normalised column and lower the search term in Python before querying with __startswith, because Django's __istartswith compiles to UPPER(col) LIKE UPPER(...) and matches no index. Decision 5 -- search identifiers, display items -- is the rule this implements, and the survey named the two guard tests that must come with it, since nothing currently stops a future annotation leaking a raw identifier value into a pulldown.

title: Publish the images, and let the chart pull them
description:
Found by a deployment review on 2026-08-22, following docs/deployment.md as somebody with a namespace and no other knowledge.

docs/deployment.md says 'helm upgrade --install ... --set image.tag=v0.1.0' and the chart renders ghcr.io/lotia/nycmesh-inventory-tng-backend:v0.1.0. Nothing in this repository has ever pushed an image: both CI image jobs use 'push: false', there are no git tags, and no workflow logs into a registry. So the migrate hook Job goes ErrImagePull, Helm blocks until --timeout, and the release fails.

Worse if the package is private: 'grep -rn imagePullSecret infra/helm/' returns nothing, so there is no way to supply a pull secret without editing the chart.

Also worth settling: ghcr.io/lotia is a personal namespace shipped as the default for an organisation's inventory system.

FIX: publish on tag, add imagePullSecrets to both Deployments and the Job, and give docs/deployment.md the build-and-push step it does not have.

title: Liveness probes the database, so a brief outage kills every pod
description:
Found by a deployment review on 2026-08-22.

backend-deployment.yaml points BOTH probes at /api/healthz, and that view executes SELECT 1. Readiness should: a pod that cannot reach the database should leave the Service. Liveness should not.

A managed PostgreSQL failover taking 70 seconds fails liveness three times at periodSeconds 20, so the kubelet kills every backend pod at once. They restart into a still-recovering database, fail again, and back off exponentially. A one-minute blip becomes a fifteen-minute outage with no pods running, and whoever is paged sees CrashLoopBackOff against a database that is by then perfectly healthy.

FIX: liveness must prove only that the process is alive. Keep /api/healthz on readiness. docs/deployment.md 'Health checks' presently states the database check as a feature and warns of nothing, so it changes with the chart.

title: Batch: setup, the two user guides, and the checks that keep them true
description:
The documentation batch: inventory-tng-61c (setup instructions for a developer and for an administrator), inventory-tng-pfw (a guide for volunteers and one for inventory administrators, with generated screenshots) and inventory-tng-a1k (the mechanism that fails the build when either goes stale).

Batched because a1k is the check over what the other two write, and because all three are read by the same person in the same sitting: somebody who has just been handed this system.
close_reason: All children completed

title: Make the setup and user guides fail the build when they go stale
description:
A separate bead rather than a line in each of the other two, because it is one mechanism serving both and because it is the part most likely to be dropped if it rides along.

THE PROBLEM IS NOT NEW HERE AND THE REPOSITORY ALREADY KNOWS IT. CLAUDE.md's second non-negotiable rule is that documentation changes with the code, and DEVELOPERS.md says of its own setup guide: 'This guide is expected to work. If a command here fails on a clean machine, that is a bug in the guide.' Nothing checks either claim. Three review passes across three batches found hand-written figures that no longer matched anything, and the answer that worked -- inventory-tng-o86.2 -- was not a rule but a test: it reads the fenced blocks out of docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md and fails when a block's labels are no longer the ones its code emits. That is the pattern to copy, twice.

FOR THE SETUP INSTRUCTIONS: execute them. The commands are already in fenced bash blocks, so the same trick applies -- extract them and run them on a clean machine in CI. A guide whose commands are run on every push cannot rot silently, and the failure names the line that is wrong. Decide how far this goes: the developer path is a container away and is plainly automatable; the administrator path needs a cluster and may only be checkable as far as 'helm template renders and the values the document names exist'. Say which parts are covered and which are not, in the document, so a reader knows which half has been proven.

FOR THE USER GUIDES: the screenshots are the perishable part, and they perish silently -- a renamed button leaves a picture that is merely wrong, with nothing failing. Two candidate mechanisms, and the bead should choose with reasons: regenerate the screenshots in CI and fail if they differ, which catches everything but is noisy on any pixel change; or assert that the elements the guide describes still exist, by driving the same Playwright scene and checking each label and control the guide names, which is quieter and catches the change that matters. The second is probably right, and it composes with the first being run on demand.

THE THIRD THING, and the one a checker cannot do: neither guide should be able to describe a role that no longer exists or omit a flow that now does. That is a review question, so it belongs in the Definition of Done rather than in CI -- and DEVELOPERS.md#definition-of-done is the single place to say it.

Do not build a documentation framework. Two tests and a CI job, in the shape the repository already uses.
acceptance_criteria: A change that breaks a documented setup command fails the build and names the command. A change that renames or removes a control the user guide describes fails the build and names the control. The Definition of Done says which documents a change has to be weighed against, and the guides themselves say which parts of them are machine-checked.
close_reason: Closed

title: A user guide for volunteers, and one for inventory administrators
description:
Two roles, two documents, because the two share almost nothing. Both as short as they can be and no shorter.

THE VOLUNTEER'S GUIDE covers one flow and its edges: scan a printed QR code, build a cart, save it, and know what happened. The edges are where a guide earns its keep -- what a per-line complaint means and how to fix one line without losing the rest; what the warning 'worth a stock count' is telling them; and the outbox, which is new and which nobody will guess at. A batch saved with no signal is held, the cart comes back empty so the next armful can be scanned, and the held batch is drawn at the top of the screen until it is in or refused. Decision 0011's amendment says why it works that way. Also worth a line: every printed QR opens the form preset to Checking Out, so returning something is not the same gesture as taking it.

THE INVENTORY ADMINISTRATOR'S GUIDE covers the things only they can do: the catalogue and what an identifier is for (a volunteer types what they call the thing, and it resolves); volunteers, and specifically merging duplicates -- a merge sets merged_into, leaves the ledger untouched, and is how the import's flagged rows get settled; the sheet_flag column on a volunteer and the one on an item, both of which are questions the import could not answer and which are answered by being emptied; locations; printing labels; and reading a balance, including that it is derived from movements and never stored.

SCREENSHOTS. Take them with the Playwright setup that already exists rather than by hand: playwright.config.ts, frontend/integration/, and seed_integration_data, which exists precisely to give the browser suite a fixed scene. A script that drives the seeded scene and captures each step is the mechanism, and it means the screenshots can be regenerated rather than re-taken. Run it headless.

FORMAT. Markdown under docs/, consistent with everything else here, with the images committed beside them. Two things to decide rather than assume: where the images live and what that does to the size of the repository, and whether the guides belong under docs/ with the architecture and the decisions or somewhere a non-developer would think to look. The reader of these two documents is not the reader of the rest of docs/, and that is worth a moment's thought.

Keep them succinct. The existing documentation in this repository is discursive because its audience is people changing the code; these two are for people using it while standing at a shelf.
design: Depends on inventory-tng-24q for the import's flags, which the administrator's guide has to explain, and on the offline outbox from inventory-tng-ykw, which is already on main.
acceptance_criteria: A volunteer who has never seen the system can complete a scan-and-save, including a failure and a save with no signal, by following the guide alone. An inventory administrator can resolve an import's flagged volunteers and items, print a label, and read a balance the same way. Every screenshot is generated by a script that can be re-run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Setup instructions a developer and an administrator can each follow start to finish
description:
Two audiences, and the current documentation serves neither completely.

A DEVELOPER running it locally. DEVELOPERS.md already has three options (all-in-Docker, native with Postgres in a container, devcontainer) and they broadly work, but a developer who follows them lands on an empty database: no catalogue, no items, no volunteers, no labels. The only seed that exists is seed_integration_data, which is deliberately gated behind an acknowledgement flag because it creates a login whose password is published in this repository -- correct for the Playwright suite and wrong as a general starting point. So the first honest thing to fix is that there is nothing to look at.

The compose setup should be MINIMALLY PRIVILEGED and should be seen to be. Worth deciding and documenting: rootless podman as a first-class path (the images are already fully qualified so it resolves without extra configuration), a non-root user in the container, a read-only root filesystem where it will hold, dropped capabilities, and no privileged ports. Whatever is chosen, the compose file should show it rather than a comment claiming it.

AN ADMINISTRATOR deploying to staging or production. docs/deployment.md and infra/helm/inventory-tng exist. What is not written down as a followable sequence is the bootstrap: which environment variables have no default and why (DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is the pattern -- see docs/architecture.md), how the migrate Job relates to the web pods, how the first administrator account comes into being, and that decision 0013 requires a second factor on the local password path so the very first sign-in cannot complete without an authenticator app. That last one is exactly the kind of step that is obvious to whoever built it and a wall to everybody else.

BOOTSTRAPPING THAT IS NOT AUTOMATED, to be enumerated honestly and then judged one by one: mise trust and mise install; copying .env.sample; the Postgres 18 volume note for anyone who ran this before August 2026; creating a superuser; enrolling that superuser's second factor; and now the sheet import, which is five commands in a required order (stage_sheet, mint_items, import_volunteers, post_ledger) or the one that composes them, import_sheet.

WEIGH AUTOMATING IT TO ONE COMMAND. The bar is that it composes commands that already exist rather than becoming a framework of its own. A script that runs mise install, writes .env from the sample, brings up Postgres, migrates, creates an administrator, seeds a small honest catalogue and prints the URL and what to do next is a good trade. A bespoke installer with its own configuration language is not. If the answer is that some step genuinely cannot be automated -- and the second factor may be one -- the script should say so at the point the human has to act, rather than the documentation saying it somewhere else.

The audience for the result includes end users too, indirectly: a volunteer or an inventory administrator meets this system only if somebody could stand it up.
design: Depends on nothing, but should be written AFTER inventory-tng-24q lands, because the import commands it has to document are part of that batch.
acceptance_criteria: A developer with neither the repository nor the toolchain can go from a clone to a working system with something in it, and an administrator can go from an empty cluster to a first sign-in, each by following one document without asking anybody. Every bootstrap step that is not automated is named in the place the reader needs it, and the decision not to automate it is stated.
close_reason: Closed

title: The importer bead still specifies from retracted figures
description:
inventory-tng-2dg gained all six classifier dependencies, and its own description still specifies the import from three figures the batch retracted.

It says '41 match nothing today ... Each becomes an ItemIdentifier row'. The brief re-partitions those: nine are case-only variants that already resolve under the sheet's case-insensitive lookup, and 32 match nothing. Minting 41 aliases would create nine rows for strings that were never broken, in the system built to stop strings being identity.

It says '~18.7% of rows are corrections, and must import as adjustments'. The brief records that 18.7% reproduces under no rule tried and that its original method is unrecorded.

It says '102 name spellings across 65 emails', which reads as a headcount and is not one.

It also points at docs/data-model.md#migrating-the-existing-sheet for a breakdown that has moved to the brief. The commit that swept 8sq and o5t for retracted figures missed the one bead the six classifiers were filed to unblock.
acceptance_criteria: 2dg states no retracted figure, cites the brief for anything rule-dependent, and its alias sizing matches the brief's partition.
close_reason: 2dg now cites the brief for each rule-dependent figure and sizes the alias table from the partition rather than from the retracted 41.

title: Move classifier-dependent figures out of decision 0008
description:
Decision 0008's Context carried eleven figures, and three review passes over one batch each found some of them unreproducible -- including two the corrections themselves introduced. The pattern is structural rather than careless: a derived statistic living as prose in a decision record has no method attached, so nobody can re-run it and everybody quotes it.

Four of the five Context bullets need a rule before they can be counted at all: which strings are unresolvable, which notes are corrections, which name a place, which name a job. Those rules are not documentation. Each is a decision the sheet importer must make about every historical row, so the rule and the figure it produces belong together and belong with the code.

0008 keeps only what needs no rule -- 52 items, 3,439 submissions, 2,455 against 984, 145 item strings, 102 name spellings -- and links to docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md for the rest. The brief states each rule beside its figure and names the command that will emit it.
acceptance_criteria: Decision 0008 states no figure that requires a classifier, the brief holds each rule beside the number it produces, and every claim the strip-down contradicted elsewhere in the record is corrected in the same change.
notes:
Six classifiers filed (2xb, e1p, 6gm, utc, a82, 5r2), each blocking both inventory-tng-2dg and the reporting command inventory-tng-6s9. The one thing no classifier can recover -- whether hardware came back -- is recorded as a non-goal on inventory-tng-8sq so it is not attempted a third time.

--- FOURTH REVIEW PASS APPLIED 2026-08-21 ---

Six defects, all in the restructure rather than in the figures, all fixed here: 0008 claimed the brief states each rule when four of six sections record that no rule is settled; the population definition was stripped out of 0008 along with the classifier figures and has been restored to the Context where the counts depending on it live, with the brief linking rather than repeating; the brief filed 145 item strings and 102 name spellings under 'needs no rule' when both are counts of distinct strings whose thing-count needs a case rule; the mesh-room figures were quoted without the compound predicate that produces them, and three plausible readings differ by 12%; kx6's notes blamed the burst gap on the submitter key when it is set entirely by the windowing rule; and two classifiers blocking P2 work were filed at P3.
close_reason: 0008 keeps only classifier-free counts; the rules and their figures live in docs/briefs/sheet-classifiers.md, and the six classifiers plus the reporting command are filed under the sheet-classifier label.

title: Re-verify every figure in decision 0008 against the workbook
description:
Decision 0008's Context is the project's most-cited evidence: the item-string mess, the check-out imbalance, the corrections share and the notes-field overloading are all quoted from it, into beads, into the stakeholder guide, and into arguments that have already changed the design once.

Four figures outside the record were checked in the course of inventory-tng-2zx and three were wrong -- a claimed 54% of check-outs carrying a note is 61%, a claimed 13% naming a node is nearer 5%, and a zip-tie distribution was out on every row. The fourth is inside 0008 itself: the Context says 'Sean mesh room 131 broome st alone accounts for 175 submissions' and that exact string appears 97 times, with roughly 156 across four spellings of the same room.

That is a poor enough hit rate that the remaining figures cannot be assumed. Each one in Context and Consequences gets reproduced from ignored/NYC Mesh - Inventory Sheet.xlsx or corrected: the 52 items and 3,439 submissions, the 145 distinct item strings and the 41 matching nothing at 160 occurrences, the 52 retired NYCM codes, 102 spellings of 65 people, 1,557 rows without an email, 2,455 check-outs against 984 check-ins, 18.7% corrections with its four enumerated counts, 136 submissions citing an NN number across 62 distinct, the 175 above, and the Consequences claim that 76% of submissions fall inside a ten-minute burst with a largest of 24.

The denominator needs settling first: the workbook's QRresponses tab holds 3,456 data rows against the record's 3,439, and every percentage depends on which filter produced the smaller number.
acceptance_criteria: Every numeric claim in decision 0008 is either reproduced from the workbook by a stated method or corrected in the record, and the method is written down so the next reader can re-run it rather than trusting the number.
notes:
VERIFICATION COMPLETE 2026-08-21. Every numeric claim in decision 0008 was counted against the QRresponses tab of the export. The population question is settled: 3,439 is the rows carrying a direction, 2,455 Checking Out plus 984 Checking In, with 17 further rows having neither. That is now stated in the record so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

Reproduced exactly, no change needed: 52 catalogued items (Fast Inventory column D, not C -- column C is the QR link and coincidentally also has 52 non-empty rows); 3,439 submissions; 2,455 check-outs against 984 check-ins; 145 distinct item strings; 52 retired NYCM codes; 41 strings not matching a catalogued name exactly (145 minus 52 NYCM minus 52 exact matches); 102 spellings of 65 people, where 65 is the count of distinct emails; the four enumerated correction counts, fixing inventory 218, updating inventory 71, inventory correction 67, inventory correct 50; 136 submissions citing an NN number; and the largest ten-minute burst at 24 items.

Reproduced within method tolerance: 45% carrying no email (1,540 within the 3,439; the record's 1,557 is the same count taken over the raw tab including the 17 directionless rows, and both round to 45%); 18.7% corrections (a broad regex gives 20.8%, and the four enumerated total 406, so the record's 643 sits inside the band its own 'and similar' allows); 76% of submissions inside a ten-minute burst by one person (77% here, the difference being how a submitter is identified when the email is blank).

Corrected in the record, three:
  * 'Sean mesh room 131 broome st alone accounts for 175 submissions' -- that exact string appears 97 times. The room is described 231 times across 41 spellings, 193 of which name 131 Broome. Replaced with the 231-across-41-spellings figure, which makes the record's own point about the notes field better than the original did.
  * '62 distinct' NN numbers -- 54. The 136 submissions figure is exact; only the distinct count was wrong.
  * '160 occurrences' for the 41 non-matching strings -- reads as a group total and is not one. The group totals 255 submissions; 160 is close to Mast straight's own 158 but matches nothing exactly. Rewritten to give both unambiguously.

No claim was found to be fabricated. The failure mode in this record is a figure counted over a slightly different population or an ambiguous antecedent, which is a different and milder problem than the discussion guide had.

--- TWO CLAIMS IN THESE NOTES CORRECTED 2026-08-21 ---

The burst attribution above is wrong. It says the 76%-versus-77% gap comes from how a submitter is identified when the email is blank, and files the largest burst of 24 under 'reproduced exactly'. Measured across all four combinations: chaining by gaps of ten minutes or less gives a largest burst of 24 under both the email key and the name key; a fixed ten-minute window gives 17 under both. The largest burst is set entirely by the windowing rule, and the submitter key moves only the percentage, by about one point. Whoever settles inventory-tng-a82 should vary the window, not the key. The brief and a82 have it right; these notes did not.

The close reason 'the counting population is now stated in the record' was true when written and was then undone within the same branch: inventory-tng-hr2 stripped the classifier-dependent figures from decision 0008 and took the population sentence with them. It has since been restored to 0008's Context, where the counts that depend on it live, and the brief links to it rather than repeating it.
close_reason: Every figure in decision 0008 reproduced or corrected; the counting population is now stated in the record.

title: Batch: review through pull requests
description:
Move the review cycle onto GitHub pull requests so that history carries at most one bead per change, and all review commentary lives in the PR rather than in messages.

This batch cannot use the workflow it builds: the message checker has to change before the batch checker can be checked by it. It lands on batch/pull-request-workflow under the old rules; the next batch is the first real run.

inventory-tng-724 joined the batch late. It is unrelated in subject -- a static files failure in CI predating all of this -- but the backend job is a required check, so nothing here could merge until it was fixed. A batch is what ships together.
